label: prf:q-heat-kernel-peter-weyl
title: Proof of q heat kernel peter weyl
html:
Proof. Schur's lemma on the irreducible Wedderburn block M_{d_\lambda(q)} forces \Delta_\xi to act by a scalar. We compute this scalar by evaluating the q-Casimir on a highest-weight vector. For H_n(q), the Casimir value equals the sum of [c(\square)]_q[c(\square) + 1]_q over cells \square \in \lambda (a classical Jucys--Murphy result, q-deformed by Ram). Multiplying by \hbar_q^2 = (1 - q^{-1})^2 yields \mu_\lambda(q).

The content-Casimir formula decomposes via the Jackson-integer shift identity (jacksonInt_mul_succ in q-heat-kernel-peter-weyl.lean):

[c]_q \cdot [c+1]_q = q \cdot [c]_q^2 + [c]_q,

yielding the equivalent form \mu_\lambda(q) = \hbar_q^2 \bigl(q \sum_{{\square \in \lambda}} [c(\square)]_q^2 + \sum_{{\square \in \lambda}} [c(\square)]_q\bigr) (muLambda_from_sq_bracket). The q \cdot [c]_q^2 term connects to the bar-symmetrised Jucys--Murphy sum \Theta_n = \sum_k (L_k + L_k^{-1}) (defined in QJucysMurphy.lean) whose block eigenvalue is \sum_{c \in \lambda} (q^{2c} + q^{-2c}), via the per-cell identity q^{2c} + q^{-2c} = (q^c - q^{-c})^2 + 2 (cosh_eq_sq_bracket_add_two). The linear term \sum [c]_q is the q-deformed first content moment, determined by \lambda alone. \square
